cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to look at another type of open addressing which is quadratic probing.
So let's say we have a hash table like this.
Now we want to insert this key and value pair to this hash table.
So here again the first thing that we are going to do we are going to pass the key to the hash function.
And we are going to get the index in which cell we are going to insert this key and value pair.
So let's say in this case it is returning four.
So we are just going to put this key and value pair at the index of four.
Because this cell is empty over here.
Now if we continue to the next key and value pair.
So let's say in this case we are inserting mango with the value of 15.
So here again we are going to pass the key to the hash function.
And let's say here again we are assuming that we are getting four.
Now if we try to insert this key and value pair to the index of four, it's going to cause collision.
Now we need to find out the next cell for inserting this one.
Now in case of linear probing we were inserting to the next cell.
But here we are going to calculate it using this equation.
So four is the index that we are getting from the hash function.
Then in the first stage, we are going to get the one and multiply it with itself.
That's why it's called quadratic.
Then we are going to take the mod of the this number with the length of the hash table that we have
over here.
So five mod seven is going to be five.
So this means that this is going to be inserted at the index of five.
Now if we try it one more time for the next key and value pair.
So let's say in this case we want to insert this one.
So here again we pass the key.
And let's say we are getting again for the index of four is already occupied.
Now if you calculate it the way that we calculated it before it's going to give us the five.
So index of five also is occupied.
So this means that it's going to continue to the second iteration.
Now in the second iteration it's going to be calculated with the square of two.
Because in the first stage it's going to give us five.
Then I'm going to skip the first.
We are going to continue to the second case, because after getting the first case, we are going to
check that if this cell is occupied, we see that it is occupied.
That's why we are going to continue to the next step.
In the next step, which is the step two.
We are going to multiply two by two and add it to the number that you are getting from the hash function,
and we are going to divide it by seven.
The remainder is going to be one.
So this means that this key and value pair inserted at the index of one.
So that's how the quadratic probing works.
Now you might be interested why we are dividing it every time by seven.
The seven is the length of the hash table that we have over here.
Now we are dividing it by seven to make the indexes smaller.
Because if we add it here, for example, we get eight and we don't have index of eight over here.
So we have to divide it by seven to make it smaller.
So that's how the logic behind the quadratic probing works.
Now when you are implementing the quadratic probing, the hash table class is going to remain the one
that we have used in case of linear probing.
So here also we have a node class and we have the constructor where we are setting the by default size
to the seven.
And we are creating with the fixed size array.
And the hash function is also same.
So that's how the hash table class looks like.
So here we have not done any modification.
Now in the next lecture we are going to use this hash class.
And inside this class we are going to implement set and get method.
So see you in the next lecture.
